newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures were hoisted off their lows by a dollar-inspired bond rally in the United States after its trade deficit narrowed and then a weak U.S. business survey pushed the contract into positive ground.
"The trade numbers were good, the Philly Fed was good, they gave the market a good cover," a trader at a French bank.
The March bond future found support at 128.10/12 when a weak start in the U.S. sent the French contract through 128.26 but then rallied to settle at 128.52, up 0.06.
Traders were decidedly unenthusiastic about the market on Thursday and said activity would tail off even more.
"The last question mark we had was over the Bundesbank. We've had that. Christmas has already started," one trader said.
Most traders said there was little chance of the contract leaving the range between 128 and 129 with some saying it would be unable even to get much beyond 128.76.

Although few analysts said they expected the Bundesbank to trim its repo rate from 3.00 percent at its last council meeting of the year, March PIBOR slipped into negative ground after the decision to leave rates unchanged was announced.
The Bundesbank decided to fix its repo rate at an unchanged 3.00 percent for the next three weeks.
But hopes that France will still be able to cut rates further, even in the face of Bundesbank intransigence, supported the Treasury's regular BTAN auction, analysts said.
The Treasury sold 18.59 billion francs of the two- and five-year benchmark BTANs with the two-year bond attracting the most interest. The two-year spread over German bonds remained close to parity.
The franc climbed slightly to 3.3783 per mark from 3.3801 on Wednesday.
